falsely told they have won a prize, lottery, or contest
fraudsters build relationships online to gain trust and create emotional connections
impersonate a grandchild, family member, or loved one claiming there is an emergency

kill_chain_signals.contact: Unsolicited phone calls, emails, text messages, or social media messages
kill_chain_signals.pretext: Fraudsters use pressure, fear, trust, or emotional manipulation; impersonate grandchild, family member, financial institutions, or law enforcement
kill_chain_signals.payment: Instructions to send money through cryptocurrency, gift cards, wire transfers, or cash; requests for upfront payments, fees, or taxes; victims pressured to move money or hand over bank cards to a courier

red_flags: Promises of guaranteed profits, winnings, or prizes
Requests for passwords, banking information, or multi-factor authentication codes
Emotional manipulation intended to create panic, fear, or urgency
key_quote: Fraudsters often use pressure, fear, trust, or emotional manipulation to convince victims to send money or share personal and financial information.
